newsitem.title: FRANCE: INSTANT VIEW-French Jan industrial output falls.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-French Jan industrial output falls.

text.p: Following are analysts' comments on a 1.2 percent month-on-month fall in French industrial production, excluding construction, in January, and a 1.0 percent fall in manufacturing output as reported by national statistics office INSEE on Friday.

Really what's important is the output number is down and even when it's just just manufacturing it's down 1.0 percent, which reverses the December bounce. It highlights the recovery will indeed be slow and growth will not pick up for some time.

You have to take account of the fact that data has been volatile recently. I don't think its worrisome for the underlying trend but the pace of recovery will nevertheless be slow in the first half. Our first-half GDP forecast was already not very good at plus 2.0 percent.
However, probably the stocks rise in the fourth quarter (of 1996) was bound to produce negative effects.
We had been expecting a total output rise of 0.8 and a 0.3 percent rise in manufacturing output.
